chunks: Ma'ani al-Akhbar and al-Amali: Muhammad ibn Ali Majlawayh narrated from his uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim, from his brother, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them) who said:
The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: … The believer takes his religion from his Lord and does not take it from his own opinion …

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Ali ibn Abi Talib)

ai.seo_question: What is the source of a believer's religion according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) underscores the Shia doctrine of *Tawqif*, asserting that the core tenets of religion are divinely fixed rather than products of human *Ra'y* (personal opinion) or *Ijtihad*. It serves as a foundational argument against the Hanafi reliance on pure analogical reasoning (*Qiyas*) for religious rulings, emphasizing that the believer's adherence is rooted in received revelation (*Naql*) from the Prophet and Imams.
